h: History and seaside fun on your doorstep
p: The market is a great place to start your day in Great Yarmouth, especially if you like to potter. Grab something to eat, have a mooch round the stalls and then head off to explore. It's handy to know your way around the centre, and the market sits right in the middle of things.

Right by the Market Place stands Great Yarmouth Minster, the Minster Church of St Nicholas, a huge and historic parish church that's well worth stepping inside. A short walk south brings you to the Time and Tide Museum, set in a former herring curing works, which tells the story of the town's fishing past in a really vivid, hands-on way. It's a cracking pick for families and a great way to understand how Yarmouth became the place it is today.

On the seafront, the Hippodrome Circus has been entertaining crowds for well over a century and still puts on shows today. The Britannia Pier and the Wellington Pier both offer classic seaside fun, while the Merrivale Model Village is a charming stop for younger kids. Animal lovers can visit the Sea Life centre on Marine Parade. At the southern end, Nelson's Monument towers over the South Denes, a tribute to the Norfolk-born naval hero. And with the Norfolk Broads just inland, you're never far from a peaceful boat trip or riverside walk if the bustle gets too much. Mixing a bit of history, a market feast and a turn on the front is a proper Yarmouth day.
